original_question: Suppose λ is singular of countable cofinality and GCH holds below λ in the sense that every θ < λ satisfies 2^θ = θ^+. Is it consistent that either \( inom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} 	o  inom{\lambda^+}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) or \( inom{2^\lambda}{\lambda} 	o  inom{2^\lambda}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
correct_elements: Your draft very closely matches the paper’s exact open problem. It correctly singles out a singular cardinal λ of countable cofinality, assumes the local GCH below λ in the form ∀θ<λ, 2^θ=θ^+, and asks about the consistency of exactly the two strong polarized relations that appear in Problem 4.7: the (λ^+, λ) case and the (2^λ, λ) case, both with two colors and exponent (1,1).
missing_details: The partition-arrow notation must be unpacked using Definition 1.1: for every coloring c:X×λ→2, there should exist A⊆X and B⊆λ with |A|=X and |B|=λ such that c is constant on A×B.
The question is a consistency question over ZFC, i.e. whether there is a model (typically obtained by forcing) in which such a λ exists.
The hypothesis should be stated exactly as λ>cf(λ)=ℵ0 and ∀θ<λ, 2^θ=θ^+; this is the paper’s precise local-GCH-below-λ formulation.
To be fully stand-alone, the two candidate cases should explicitly specify the sizes of the monochromatic rectangles: |A|=λ^+ in the first case and |A|=2^λ in the second, always with |B|=λ.
The paper phrases this as an either/or consistency problem; it does not ask for both relations simultaneously under the local GCH assumption.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that there exists a singular cardinal λ with cf(λ)=ω and 2^θ=θ^+ for every θ<λ such that at least one of the following strong polarized partition relations holds: (λ^+, λ) → (λ^+, λ)^{1,1}_2, meaning that every coloring c:λ^+×λ→2 has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A|=λ^+ and |B|=λ; or (2^λ, λ) → (2^λ, λ)^{1,1}_2, meaning that every coloring c:2^λ×λ→2 has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A|=2^λ and |B|=λ?
justification: This is essentially Problem 4.7 verbatim. The paper first asks in Problem 4.6 whether these same two strong polarized relations are consistent for a strong limit singular λ in general, then immediately sharpens the question by observing that when cf(λ)=ω one may violate the local continuum hypothesis at λ while still keeping 2^θ=θ^+ below λ, leading exactly to Problem 4.7. Definition 1.1 is needed to make the arrow notation self-contained. Section 5 confirms that the two cases λ^+ and 2^λ are the precise special cases the authors regard as most interesting in the later main theorem, although the later positive results are obtained under different hypotheses and so do not replace Problem 4.7.
